newsitem.title: USA: WTC anticipates loss for second quarter. [CORRECTED 19:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: WTC anticipates loss for second quarter. [CORRECTED 19:40 GMT]

text.p: WTC Industries Inc, a water filtration and purification products maker, said Wednesday it expects to report a loss for the second quarter.
"At this time, I'm anticipating a loss for the quarter," chief financial officer Greg Jensen told Reuters in a telephone interview.
The company also said it expects net sales in June will likely be substantially below the previous three months. (Corrects by Inserting word "likely").
Sales were $503,400 in March, $409,300 in April and $637,300 in May, the company said. (Corrects third month to May.)
In the second quarter of 1996, the company reported a net loss of $1.1 million, or $0.10 a share.
WTC also said Wednesday it has proposed to exchange stock and warrants for about $1.5 million in promissory notes, which Jensen said would help improve the balance sheet.
The exchange would save the company about $152,000 a year in interest and WTC hopes to complete the conversion by mid-July. The notes were issued in 1994.

The company is offering the holders of the notes the right to convert each $100,000 in principal of the 1994 notes to 80,000 shares and a new three-year redeemable stock purchase warrant to purchase 20,000 shares at an exercise price of $1.25 a share, the company said in a news release.
The company's offer is subject to the condition that the holders of at least $1 million in principal amount of the 1994 notes accept the company's offer, WTC said.
